extracted.intended_audience: applicants, IP practitioners, and government authorities dealing with industrial property registration and enforcement in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for filing, examining, granting, using, and enforcing industrial property rights (inventions, designs, marks, geographical indications, layout-designs, business secrets) under Vietnamese law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptions of peculiar characteristics for geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of peculiar characteristics must include essential contents describing the relevant product, methods, evidence of origin, production methods, relationship to natural conditions, and self-control mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) description of the relevant product including raw materials and physical, chemical, microbiological and perceptive characteristics; (b) methods of determination of the geographical area corresponding to the GI; (c) evidence proving the product originates from that geographical area (per Article 79); (d) descriptions of local and stable methods of production and processing; (dd) information on the relationship between peculiar characteristics/quality/reputation and natural conditions (per Article 79); (e) information on the self-control mechanism of the product's peculiar characteristics or quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney essential contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A written power of attorney is required for authority to carry out industrial property procedures and must include specified essential contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include: full name and address of principal and attorney; scope of authority; validity term; date of the power of attorney; signature and seal (if any). A power with no validity term is valid indefinitely until principal declares termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents for receiving industrial property registration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be received only if it contains specified documents and information identifying the applicant and the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: (a) a request for registration with adequate information to identify the applicant and, for marks, a sample and list of goods/services; (b) specifications — inventions must include specification and scope of protection, industrial designs must include photos/drawings, GIs must include descriptions of peculiar characteristics; (c) receipt of prescribed fees and charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date is the date the application is received by the State administrative authority or the international filing date for treaty applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are examined as to form to verify formal validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal examination checks fulfillment of formality requirements, eligibility of subject matter, applicant's right to register, correct mode of filing, and payment of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for formal invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is not formally valid if it falls under enumerated circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include: (a) application does not fulfill formality requirements; (b) subject matter not eligible for protection; (c) applicant lacks right to registration (e.g., co-owners disagree); (d) filed contrary to the prescribed mode of filing; (d’) failure to pay fees and charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for formally invalid applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority must follow procedural steps when an application is formally invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority shall serve a notice of intended refusal stating reasons and a time limit to overcome defects or to object; if defects are not overcome or objection unjustified, serve a notice of refusal; where defects are overcome or objection justified, carry out acceptance procedures (or grant for layout-design where applicable). A mark application refused as formally invalid is considered never filed except for priority claim purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted applications are published according to specified timelines depending on IP type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions: publication in the 19th month from filing or priority date (or earlier on request). Industrial designs, marks, and geographical indications: published within 2 months from acceptance as formally valid. Layout-design applications: allow direct access without reproduction; basic info on layout-design and protection title published within 2 months from grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention and industrial design applications must be kept secret until publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff disclosing such information will be disciplined and must compensate for damages to the applicant under law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third parties' opinions during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: From publication until the decision on grant, any third party may present written opinions about grant or refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinions must be in written form and be accompanied by materials or specify sources of information used for proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for requesting substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for substantive examination of invention applications must be made within statutory time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General inventions: within 42 months from filing date or priority date. Utility solution patent requests: within 36 months. Failure to request substantive examination within the time limit results in the application being regarded as withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Which applications are examined as to substance is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination applies to: (a) invention applications accepted as formally valid for which a request for substantive examination has been filed; (b) industrial design, mark and geographical indication applications accepted as formally valid. Layout-design registration applications are not examined as to substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to amend, supplement, divide, convert, and record changes before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the authority issues a notice of refusal or decision to grant, applicants have specified procedural rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may amend or supplement the application, divide the application, request recording changes in name or address, request recording changes in applicant via assignment/inheritance/authority decision, and convert between invention patent and utility solution patent requests. Fees and charges apply for these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraints on amendments and supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment or supplement must not expand the scope or change the substance of the claimed subject matter and must ensure unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that expand disclosure or change substance are prohibited; unity of the application must be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division preserves original filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is divided, the filing date of the divided application is that of the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal procedure and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may withdraw applications in writing and withdrawal has specified procedural effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal can be declared in the applicant's own name or through an IP representative if the power of attorney expressly grants withdrawal authority. Upon withdrawal, further procedures are suspended; fees/charges already paid for uncommenced procedures may be refunded on request. Applications withdrawn or regarded as withdrawn before publication (inventions/designs) and withdrawn mark applications are considered never filed except as basis for priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusal to grant Protection Titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority shall refuse to grant a Protection Title when specified substantive or formal conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal grounds include: (a) subject matter does not fulfill protection requirements; (b) application satisfies conditions but is not the earliest filing/priority application; (c) application falls under Article 90.1 but applicants do not reach consensus. For layout-designs, grant shall be refused if formality requirements are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for refusal to grant Protection Titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps when an application is to be refused are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve notice of intended refusal with reasons and time limit to oppose; if applicant has no objection or objection is unjustified, serve notice of refusal; if applicant has a justifiable objection, grant Protection Title and enter in register. If a protest is made against intention to grant, re-examine the protested matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of Protection Titles and entry into register
rubrics_metrics.description: If application does not fall under refusal grounds and fees are paid, authority shall grant and acknowledge the Protection Title in the National Register for Industrial Property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for processing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory time limits for form and substantive examination and for re-examination are set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form examination: within 1 month from filing date. Substance examination: inventions — within 12 months from publication or from request date; industrial designs, marks, GIs — within 6 months from publication. Re-examination time limit equals two-thirds of initial examination time (extendable in complicated cases). Time allowed for amendments/supplements is excluded from these time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications must comply with treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed under treaties must comply with the relevant international treaty and implementing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government shall provide guidelines for implementing provisions on international applications and their processing in accordance with the principles of the Chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership rules for industrial property objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines who is the owner of various industrial property objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner of an invention, industrial design or layout design is the grantee of a Protection Title. Owner of a mark is grantee of Protection Title, holder of internationally registered mark as recognized by competent agency, or a well-known mark owner. Trade name owner is the person who legally uses it in business. Business secret owner is who legally acquired and keeps it secret. The State is owner of Vietnam's geographical indications and grants rights to use/manage to relevant organizations or individuals; the State may manage directly or grant representation to an organization acting on behalf of users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' personal and property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of inventions, industrial designs and layout designs have personal rights to attribution and property rights to remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal rights: to be named as author in patents/certificates and in publications; property right: right to remuneration according to Article 135 of the Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owners' property rights (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners of industrial property objects have rights to use, to prohibit others from using, and to dispose of the industrial property object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations or individuals granted the right to use/manage GIs also have the right to allow others to use and to prohibit others from using GIs consistent with these clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes: manufacturing the protected product; applying the protected process; exploiting uses of the protected product or products obtained by the protected process; circulating, advertising, offering, storing for circulation such products; importing such products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of an industrial design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes: manufacturing products whose appearance embodies the protected industrial design; putting into circulation, advertising, offering, storing for circulation such products; importing such products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of a layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes: reproducing the layout-design or manufacturing an integrated circuit incorporating the protected layout-design; selling, leasing, advertising, offering or storing copies or articles incorporating such integrated circuits; importing copies or articles incorporating such layout-design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for business secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of a business secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes: applying the business secret to manufacture products, supply services or trade; selling, advertising, storing for sale and importing products obtained by applying the business secret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of a mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes: affixing the protected mark to goods, packages, business means or service materials and transaction papers; circulating, offering, advertising and storing goods bearing the protected mark; importing goods or services bearing the protected mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of a trade name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes acts for commercial purposes using the trade name in business activities, transaction documents, shop-signs, products, packages and advertisements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use' for geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts that constitute the use of a geographical indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use includes: affixing the protected GI to goods or packaging, business means and transaction documents during business activities; circulating, offering, advertising and storing goods bearing the protected GI; importing goods bearing the protected GI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions limiting right to prevent others' use (limitations to exclusivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners cannot prevent certain uses that fall under enumerated exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: personal or non-commercial use; evaluation, analysis, research, teaching, testing, pilot production, developing info to carry out licensing/marketing procedures; exhaustion of rights (goods legally put on the market, including in foreign markets, except those put into foreign markets by persons other than the mark owner or licensee); maintaining operation of a foreign vehicle in transit; prior user rights; use authorized by state authorities (Articles 145/146); using a layout-design when one is unaware of its protection; using marks identical/similar to a protected GI if protection for the mark was acquired truthfully before the GI filing date; truthful use of names/descriptive symbols about type, quantity, quality, utility, value, geographical origin and other specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of infringement of inventions, industrial designs and layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists acts considered infringement for inventions, industrial designs and layout designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement includes: using the protected invention/design/layout (or an insufficiently different design, or original part of layout) during the Protection Title term without owner's permission; using the invention/design/layout without paying compensation as provided for provisional rights under Article 131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts infringing business secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists acts considered infringements of business secret rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: accessing or acquiring information embodied in a business secret by acting against secret-keeping measures; disclosing or using business secret info without permission; breaching secret-keeping contracts or deceiving/inducing/bribing/forcing/seducing/abusing trust to access or disclose; accessing information submitted by another under licensing/marketing procedures by actions against secret-keeping measures by competent agencies; using/disclosing a business secret while knowing or being obliged to know it was acquired by such illicit acts; failure to perform secret-keeping obligations (Article 128). Lawful controller includes owner, lawful licensee or manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to keep secrecy of test data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities must protect test data/business secret data submitted for certain licensing procedures and observe a limited exclusivity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where law requires submission of test data for pharmaceutical or agricultural chemical product licensing and applicant requests secrecy, the authority must take measures so the data are neither used for unfair commercial purposes nor disclosed except where necessary to protect the public. From submission to end of 5 years from license grant, the authority shall not grant a license to a subsequent applicant whose application uses the secret data without permission of the submitter, except as provided in Article 125.3(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts infringing marks, trade names and geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific acts that constitute infringement of marks, trade names and GIs are enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks: (a) using signs identical with a protected mark for identical goods/services in the registered list; (b) using identical signs for similar/related goods/services if likely to cause confusion; (c) using similar signs for identical/similar/related goods/services if likely to cause confusion; (d) using signs identical/similar to a well-known mark, including translations/transliterations, for any goods/services (even dissimilar) if likely to cause confusion or false impression of relationship. Trade name: using commercial indications identical/similar to another's trade name used before that causes confusion as to business entity or activities. Geographical indications: (a) using GI for products not satisfying the peculiar characteristics and quality even if originating from the area; (b) using GI for similar products to take advantage of reputation; (c) using sign identical/similar to GI for products not originating from the area causing consumer deception; (d) using protected GIs of wines/spirits for wines/spirits not originating in the territory even if true origin is indicated or words like 'type', 'imitation' are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of unfair competition and definition of commercial indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates acts considered unfair competition and defines commercial indications and their uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfair competition acts include: using commercial indications causing confusion as to business entities or commercial source; causing confusion as to origin, production method, feature, quality, quantity or other characteristics or conditions for provision of goods/services; improper use of a mark protected abroad by a former representative/agent; registering/using a domain name identical/confusingly similar to a protected trade name/mark/GI to possess or benefit from or prejudice reputation/goodwill. 'Commercial indications' include signs and information guiding trade: marks, trade names, business symbols, slogans, GIs, package/label designs, etc. 'Use' includes affixing on goods, packaging, transaction documents and advertising; selling, advertising, storing, importing goods affixed with such commercial indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights to inventions, industrial designs and layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may assert provisional rights against third-party commercial use during pendency and claim remuneration if the right is later granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant knows another is using the invention/design/layout commercially without prior user right, applicant may serve written notice specifying filing and publication dates so the user may terminate or continue use. For layout-designs commercially exploited before grant by the person having the right to registration, they may serve such notice. If user continues use and a Protection Title is later issued, the owner may request remuneration equivalent to licensing fees for the relevant scope and period of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors limiting industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates statutory factors that limit industrial property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits include: rights of prior users; obligations of owners such as paying remuneration to authors and the duty to use the invention/mark; requirements to transfer rights to use inventions under State authority decisions.
